scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

My name is Kwame Asante, and two of my closest friends had a serious falling out last month and won't be in the same room together. We have a community gathering coming up that needs both of them. Do you think it's my responsibility to fix this?

Hello Kwame Asante! I'm glad you reached out for advice. It's understandable that you're concerned about your friends' situation, especially with the community gathering coming up. While it's natural to want to help your friends resolve their issues, it's essential to consider whether it's truly your responsibility to "fix" the situation. Here are some points to ponder: 1. **You can't force reconciliation**: Ultimately, it's up to your friends to work through their differences and decide whether they want to repair their relationship. You can't force them to talk or reconcile if they're not ready. 2. **Respect their boundaries**: If your friends have decided to avoid each other, it's crucial to respect their boundaries and not push them to interact if they're not comfortable doing so. 3. **Your role is to support, not mediate**: As a friend, you can offer emotional support and a listening ear to both parties, but it's not your job to mediate their conflict or try to "fix" the situation. 4. **Focus on the community gathering**: Instead of trying to resolve the conflict, you could focus on finding ways to make the community gathering successful and enjoyable for everyone involved, regardless of your friends' relationship status. That being said, if you feel that your friends' conflict is affecting the community or the gathering, you could consider having an open and honest conversation with both of them separately. You might express your concerns and encourage them to find a way to coexist peacefully, at least for the sake of the community event. Remember, Kwame, your primary responsibility is to be a good friend and support your friends individually. It's not your job to fix their conflict, but rather to be a positive influence and help create a welcoming environment for everyone. How do you feel about this situation, and what do you think you might do to support your friends and the community gathering?

While it's understandable that you wanted to simplify your Switch experience, deleting his profile without warning or discussing it with him was thoughtless and inconsiderate. Your stepbrother had grown attached to playing on your Switch, and his save was important to him. By deleting his profile, you not only erased his progress but also disregarded his emotional investment in the game. It's no wonder he was upset and felt hurt by your actions. It's also worth noting that you had created the profile for him in the first place, which implies that you were willing to share your Switch with him. Deleting his profile without a second thought undermines that initial gesture of kindness and suggests that you didn't value his gaming experience or his feelings. In hindsight, it would have been better to talk to your stepbrother about your concerns and find a solution that worked for both of you, such as creating a new profile or finding a way to manage the existing one.
